request: Remove the largest radius that is all around the part and replace it by the same size radius as others. That means in cross section all radiuses will be the same for the profile.

actions.target: The largest radius extending all around the part.
actions.relational_constraint: The targeted radius must be the circumferential radius that extends all around the part.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify which existing radius is the largest and verify which radius feature extends all around the part.
steps: Identify the targeted feature as the continuous radius-10 outer bullnose in Section S04, not the radius-63 outer planform corners in S04 or the radius-50 aperture corners in S02. The latter radii control the rounded-rectangular path in plan view, while the radius-10 bullnose is the largest edge radius visible in a section normal to the perimeter.

Confirm continuity of the radius-10 feature around the complete perimeter by tracing face codes 0042 through 0049: lower-left bullnose corner 0042, bottom bullnose rail 0043, lower-right bullnose corner 0044, right bullnose rail 0045, upper-right bullnose corner 0046, top bullnose rail 0047, upper-left bullnose corner 0048, and left bullnose rail 0049.

In the parametric feature history, locate the perimeter fillet or bullnose feature that generated the eight radius-10 faces and suppress, delete, or roll back that feature while retaining the underlying outer structural shell.

If the model is imported without editable feature history, select the complete tangent-connected set of bullnose faces 0042-0049 and use Delete Face with heal to extend the adjacent supporting surfaces until they intersect. Preserve the outer wall faces 0034-0041 and the adjoining annular-land geometry.

Inspect a section plane normal to any straight perimeter rail, preferably through the midpoint of the top or bottom rail, and verify that the radius-10 arc has been removed and that the adjacent profile surfaces form a clean, filletable intersection.

Check all four rounded planform corners after removal. The outer rounded-rectangle path and its nominal radius-63 corner geometry must remain unchanged; only the through-thickness bullnose radius is to be removed.
Rebuild or repair any corner intersections created by removing the toroidal bullnose patches so the entire perimeter presents one continuous edge chain suitable for a new constant-radius fillet.

parameters.radius_size: same size as the other radii

actions.target: The geometry from which the largest all-around radius was removed.
actions.relational_constraint: The replacement radius must extend over the same all-around region and equal the common radius size of the other profile radii, so all radii are equal in cross section.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the other radii referenced by 'others,' determine their common radius value, and identify the cross-sectional profile used to verify equality.
steps: Use the documented radius-2 transitions in Sections S01 and S03 as the dimensional reference. The front outer and inner perimeter fillets in S01 and the rear inner perimeter fillets in S03 all have a common radius of 2 mm, establishing 2 mm as the intended common cross-sectional profile radius.

Do not use the radius-50 inner aperture corners or radius-63 outer shell corners as the replacement value because those are in-plane path radii rather than edge radii in the through-thickness profile.

Create a section plane normal to a straight perimeter rail and intersecting the frame thickness. Project the adjacent outer-wall and land boundaries into the section sketch to verify the intended profile and available material.

If profile reconstruction is required, replace the removed radius-10 arc in the section sketch with a tangent arc constrained to 2 mm. Apply tangency constraints to both adjoining profile segments and preserve the existing land offsets and overall frame path.

For a native solid-edge operation, select the complete perimeter edge chain produced by removal of the bullnose. Enable tangent propagation or loop selection so the operation runs along all four straight rails and through all four rounded corners without interruption.

Apply a constant-radius fillet of 2 mm to the selected all-around edge chain. The resulting straight-rail patches will be cylindrical and the four corner transition patches will be toroidal, replacing the same continuous region formerly represented by face codes 0042-0049.

If the CAD kernel cannot propagate the fillet through the rounded corners, construct a 2 mm tangent section arc and sweep it along the existing rounded-rectangular perimeter path. Use solid add or solid trim as appropriate, then union and heal the result into a single watertight body.

Maintain the nominal radius-63 outer corner path, the radius-50 inner aperture path, the front seating land, the rear retaining land, and the inner locating wall. The edit must change only the cross-sectional perimeter bullnose from radius 10 mm to radius 2 mm.

Inspect normal sections through the top, bottom, left, and right straight rails and through each planform corner. Verify that the replacement radius is consistently 2 mm and tangent to its adjacent surfaces everywhere.

Confirm that the final part remains a single closed solid with an uninterrupted perimeter, no sliver faces, no self-intersections, and no discontinuities at the transitions between cylindrical rail fillets and toroidal corner fillets.

Perform a final cross-sectional comparison against the radius-2 front and rear profile transitions to verify the design intention that all edge radii in the through-thickness profile are the same size.

intention: Make all radii in the cross-sectional profile the same size.
